name: Normies Pixel Check
description: Live on-chain #PIXEL truth for Normies, not marketplace lag. How many pixels a Normie really holds (and whether any were just pulled), which open offers sit on Normies that lost their pixels, listings that show more pixels than they have, who a wallet approved to spend its #PIXEL, whether an address is an official Normies contract, and whether buying pixels on the Pixel Market beats burning floor Normies. Read-only: never asks for keys, seeds or signatures. Open access. Independent community tool, not made or endorsed by the Normies team.

token.description: Normie token ID. Returns the live pixels attached on chain, the locked / free split, recent pixel withdrawals, the listing price and the open offers on it.

wallet.description: 0x address or .eth name. Returns every open Normies item offer that wallet made, each next to that Normie's live pixels, risky ones first.

listings.description: true returns the cheapest listings whose live pixels are below what OpenSea shows or below our census.

approvals.description: 0x address or .eth name. Returns every spender that wallet approved for #PIXEL, with live amounts and official labels.

contract.description: 0x address. Says whether it is on the official Normies contract list.

calc.description: Buy-smart calculator: 'pixels' = how many pixels you want, 'eth' = how much ETH you want to spend. Requires amount.

amount.description: With calc=pixels a whole number of pixels (up to 1000000); with calc=eth an ETH budget (up to 1000).

outputs.description: Pass exactly one of token, wallet, listings, approvals, contract or calc (+ amount). The shape follows the question asked. Errors are JSON {error, code, retryable}.

kind.description: 'ok' or 'error' for wallet, listings and approvals checks

answer.description: calc only: the plan with verdict burn | gamble | market | unknown, market and burn costs in ETH, and the saving

official.description: contract only: true when the address is an official Normies contract

checkedAt.description: ISO timestamp of the read (calc answers carry asOf instead)
